steps.h: Point your camera at the code
steps.b: Or open coachkenny.org/decks and tap this deck.
Same slides as the projector — swipe at your own pace.
The link opens slide 1 of this Coach OS walkthrough.

slides.note: Hold here until every phone shows the deck.

cards.b: Built to use standing on a field with one hand. No app to install — it is a website you can save to your home screen.
You see your roster, your schedule, your athletes. Nothing from anybody else’s team.
When the athletic director updates a practice or adds a player, it is on your screen. Nobody has to resend anything.
Your team, roster and schedule are already loaded before you log in the first time.

slides.title: Sign in

steps.b: No username, no password to forget. Three digits and you are in.
On your own phone you will usually stay signed in, so it is one tap next time.
That is the home base. Everything else is a tab across the top.
Check with the athletic director — PINs are issued per team.

slides.note: Save athleticsos.io/coach to your phone's home screen and it opens like an app.

cards.b: Every athlete on your team, with jersey info and whether their registration and fees are cleared.
During tryouts, the athletes checking in right now — and where you rate them.
Take attendance at practice in a few taps, and see the whole season at a glance.
Your practices and games, upcoming and past.
Report a final score after a game, and turn a paper stat sheet into real numbers.
Drills you can run, with setup, coaching cues and video.
Live playing-time tracker so every kid gets their minutes.
Your coaching staff, and the players and families on your team.

slides.title: Athletes appear as they check in

steps.b: It turns into Tryouts (12) and the number climbs as athletes check in at the table.
Every few seconds, even if you are sitting on a different tab.
The check-in table decides which teams each athlete is sent to, so your list stays clean.
Tryout number, first name and grade — enough to find them on the floor.

slides.note: If an athlete is standing in front of you but not on your screen, they have not checked in at the table yet.

slides.title: Rate athletes live

steps.b: Tap the stars on the athlete’s card. Change it any time during the session.
“Great hands, needs conditioning” beats trying to remember number 34 later.
By check-in order to find someone fast, or by rating to see your board taking shape.
Every coach rates on their own hub. Another coach cannot see your stars or notes.

slides.note: It saves as you tap. There is no submit button and nothing to lose if your phone locks.

steps.b: Yellow while everyone is gathering, green when the draft goes live.
Do this in the lobby so the draft can start with everyone in.
It snakes — last pick in a round picks first in the next, so nobody is stuck picking last every time.
You get a set amount of time on your turn. If it runs out the draft moves on, so have your board ready.
This is why rating live during tryouts matters — your stars are what you draft from.
Numbers and sizes, so you are not texting for them at uniform handout.
Flags show you who is not fully cleared yet. You do not chase it — but you know before game day.
Anything the office has flagged that you should know about an athlete.

slides.title: Take attendance at practice

steps.b: Tap present for who showed. Mark excused when a parent let you know. Anyone left unmarked is absent.
You pick from your actual scheduled practices, so records line up with the calendar.
See a whole athlete’s attendance at a glance — useful for the playing-time and eligibility conversations.

slides.note: Do it at practice, not after. It is faster and you will not misremember who was there.

steps.b: Enter the opponent, choose quarters or halves, how long each period is, and how many players are on the floor at once.
Equal playing time gives every athlete a target. Or track by practice attendance instead.
The clock runs and each athlete’s minutes add up. You can see at a glance who is short.
Finished games are archived, so if a parent asks how much their kid played, you have the answer.
Opponent, our score, and a notes box for anything the athletic director should know.
Upload a picture of the paper sheet and it is read into player stats automatically — no typing rows in.
Individual and season totals for your team, without a spreadsheet.
Practices and games, split into upcoming and past, with cancellations marked. It is the same calendar the office edits, so it is never stale.
Your head and assistant coaches, plus players and families — so you are not digging for a phone number at 6pm.

steps.h: Every drill is laid out the same
steps.b: What skill it builds, how to set it up, the main coaching cues, how to run it, and what to watch for.
Some drills include a clip so you can see it before you teach it.
Find something for the thing your team is actually bad at this week.
The library is built out for flag football right now. Other sports say “coming soon” until theirs is added.

items: Save it to your phone’s home screen.
Roster is home. Tabs across the top for everything else.
Check Schedule for practice and game changes.
Watch the Tryouts tab go green — athletes appear as they check in.
Rate 1–5 stars and take notes while you watch.
Sort by rating to build your board.
Tap Join Draft in the lobby, and be ready — your turn is on a clock.
Run PT Tracker during games so minutes are fair and provable.
Photograph the stat sheet instead of typing it.
